headline: SILVER STORM HITS 661 g/t Ag.Eq OVER 3.7m AT SAN MARCOS — 1,461 g/t Ag.Eq Bonanza Core; La Parrilla Oxide Zone Expands as Silver Tests $60 (CVE:SVRS)
snippet: Silver Storm Mining Ltd. (CVE:SVRS) released July 22 drill results from the oxide zones of the past-producing San Marcos mine at its La Parrilla Silver Mine Complex in Durango, Mexico, with hole IDP-SM-26-003A returning 661 g/t Ag.Eq over 3.70 metres including a 1,231 g/t Ag.Eq high-grade core over 1.60 m, and EDP-SM-26-006 cutting 328 g/t Ag.Eq over 15.35 metres with a 1,461 g/t Ag.Eq bonanza over 2.00 m. With 93 holes and ~9,395 metres completed at San Marcos year-to-date, the company is building toward a resource update while spot silver tests the psychologically important $60 per ounce level.

headline: NEVADA GEOTECHS DRILL FOR PERMITS, FIND GOLD INSTEAD — Lahontan Hits 31m at 0.90 g/t Au Oxide Below Calvada Pit Shell; Heap-Leach Project (CVE:LG)
snippet: Lahontan Gold Corp. (CVE:LG) disclosed July 22 that a geotechnical diamond drill hole at Calvada Central — bored for mine permitting data at the Santa Fe Mine Project in Esmeralda County, Nevada — intersected 30.8 metres grading 0.93 g/t Au Eq oxide from 94.8m to 125.6m depth, below the current resource pit outline, including a high-grade 10.7-metre interval at 2.18 g/t Au Eq and a 1.4-metre bonanza at 3.25 g/t Au. Management says the below-pit intercept suggests resource extension potential and plans dedicated step-out holes to test it in the coming quarter.

headline: PUMA'S INAUGURAL McKENZIE DRILL HITS 42 g/t Au BONANZA VEINS IN NEW BRUNSWICK — High-Grade Orogenic Gold System Confirmed in First 2,721m (CVE:PUMA)
snippet: Puma Exploration Inc. (CVE:PUMA) reported July 21 that its inaugural 2,721-metre diamond drill program at the RIM Gold Zone of the McKenzie Gold Project in Northern New Brunswick confirmed a high-grade orogenic gold system, with multiple shear and extension vein structures returning visible gold at 42.60 g/t Au over 0.25m, 21.86 g/t Au over 0.30m, 15.55 g/t Au over 0.30m, and 13.41 g/t Au over 0.25m within a broader 5-to-20-metre lower-grade envelope. The high-grade results validated management's Costerfield-style thesis for McKenzie and prompted the company to add a second drill rig.

headline: HM EXPLORATION CONFIRMS BLIND VMS LENS IN NEWFOUNDLAND — 23m at 1.2% Cu, 1.7% Zn, 10.7 g/t Ag; Two Sulphide Lenses Defined, Phase 2 Planned (CVE:HM)
snippet: HM Exploration Corp. (CVE:HM) released July 21 assay results from the first seven holes of its Phase One program at the Lewis Pilley's Project in Newfoundland, confirming polymetallic VMS-style mineralization across both an upper and lower sulphide lens in a deposit with no surface expression. Best results include 23 metres at 1.2% Cu, 1.7% Zn, 10.7 g/t Ag, and 0.25 g/t Au, with higher-grade zones reaching 2.03% Cu, 16.35 g/t Ag, and 0.38 g/t Au over 8.18m; Phase Two drilling is in planning for fall 2026 based on the confirmed strike continuity.

headline: NOVO CONFIRMS SILVER-ANTIMONY-ZINC SYSTEM AT WYLOO — 600m Vera Anomaly, 27m Zinc Halo Found in Maiden Pilbara Drill; Assays Pending (TSX:NVO)
snippet: Novo Resources Corp. (TSX:NVO) completed its maiden drill program at the Wyloo Gold-Silver-Antimony Project in southern Pilbara, Western Australia on July 21, confirming a genuine hydrothermal system with silver and antimony grades from surface at Wyloo SE and a broad 27-metre zinc zone grading above 0.10% Zn; the newly identified Vera prospect hosts a 260m-wide by 600m-long antimony-arsenic soil anomaly that extends well beyond what was drilled. Assays are pending, but visual alteration — strong sericite and chlorite with anomalous arsenic and antimony — validates the target within 100km of Novo's established Pilbara gold portfolio.

headline: PBoC BOUGHT 14.93 TONNES OF GOLD IN JUNE — Biggest Single-Month Addition Since 2023, Mid-Selloff; State Street Puts $4,750-$5,500 at 70% Probability
snippet: State Street Investment Management's July 2026 Monthly Gold Monitor reports that the People's Bank of China purchased 14.93 tonnes of gold in June alone — the largest single-month PBoC addition since 2023 — occurring during gold's steepest quarterly correction since 2013, which State Street interprets as a structural demand signal. The report assigns a 70% base-case probability to gold reaching $4,750–$5,500 per ounce within six to nine months, anchored by global sovereign debt at an all-time high of $353 trillion and sustained central bank accumulation; the 25% scenario sees gold consolidating in the $4,000–$4,750 range pending Fed clarity.

headline: GOLD AT $4,140 WITH SIX DAYS TO FOMC — 89% Hold Probability Is Priced In; Warsh's Language, Not the Rate, Is the Real Market Mover
snippet: With gold trading near $4,140 and the July 28-29 FOMC meeting six days away, Allegiance Gold argues that the rate decision itself is essentially fully priced at an 89% hold probability per CME FedWatch — and that the real market risk is Fed Chair Kevin Warsh's post-meeting tone, where even modestly hawkish forward guidance could lift real yields and cap the metal's current geopolitical-bid rally. A hold with neutral language would likely allow gold to extend toward $4,300-$4,400 in August; hawkish language or a rate hike would risk a retest of the $4,000 technical support that held twice in early-to-mid July.

headline: ED STEER: COMMERCIALS STEPPING ASIDE IS THE TELL — Silver $60 Break Has Real Legs If COMEX Banks Don't Defend (GoldSeek)
snippet: GoldSeek columnist Ed Steer argues that gold and silver are positioned for a major surge based on current COMEX positioning, where commercial traders (large bank short-sellers who historically cap rallies) have failed to aggressively defend against the recent run from the $4,000 gold and $56 silver lows — a signal he reads as deliberate disengagement rather than failed intervention. Steer contends that when commercial traders allow a precious metals rally to run without heavy short-side pressure, the moves tend to be large and fast, and projects that if they continue to stand aside on silver's $60 breakout attempt, the path to $70-$80 per ounce opens on a sixth consecutive deficit year.

headline: SILVER'S STRUCTURAL CASE IS IMPECCABLE — BUT FOMC JULY 29 STILL THE GATEKEEPER; Sixth Deficit Year Means Nothing Without a Fed Pivot
snippet: Crux Investor argues that silver's sixth consecutive supply deficit of 46.3 million ounces, 58% industrial demand share, and gold-silver ratio near the 50-year top at 69.2:1 build a compelling structural bull case — but that Fed rate expectations, not physical fundamentals, have been the dominant near-term price driver all year. With a sub-15% probability assigned to a July 29 rate hike, the FOMC hold outcome is the catalyst Crux Investor identifies as the trigger for silver to break and hold above $60, after which the structural deficit narrative can take over and potentially drive the next leg to $65-$70.

headline: BATTERY METALS RECOVERY STALLS HALFWAY — Lithium, Cobalt, Nickel All Off Lows But EV Demand Disappoints West; Supply Cuts Doing All the Lifting
snippet: A Mining.com analysis finds that lithium, cobalt, and nickel prices have recovered from their 2024-2025 lows primarily via supply restraint — Congo's cobalt export ban since February 2025, Indonesian nickel quotas — rather than demand recovery, leaving the rebound structurally fragile. With US and European EV adoption running 15-20% below 2023 forecasts while Chinese EV sales grow robustly, the analysis warns that any policy relaxation on supply could quickly overshoot a demand base that has not grown fast enough to justify the supply discipline needed to keep battery metal prices at current levels.
